title: Detecting Magnons with High Resolution Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy
content: A decade after its first demonstration, high-resolution electron-energy-loss spectroscopy (vibrational-EELS) in a scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) has pushed the capabilities of analytical electron microscopy [1]. Phonons, the quanta of lattice vibrations can now be detected at atomic resolution [2], along with their dispersion in momentum space [3], and related to local atomic structure and chemistry. Magnons are quasiparticles representing the collective excitation of spins in magnetic materials. Magnons, along with hybrid magnon-phonon quasiparticles (magnon polarons), are the basis for the operation of new spin wave transfer logic devices. They occupy the same spectral window as phonon modes, ranging from a few to a few hundred meV in solid-state materials, suggesting that STEM-EELS may offer the ability to detect them at the nanoscale. This would open new avenues for studying spin wave propagation in magnetic materials, their dispersions, and their modifications arising from nanoscale structural or chemical defects.
